newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac opens Paris Japanese culture centre.
newsitem.headline: Chirac opens Paris Japanese culture centre.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Tuesday inaugurated a major Japanese cultural centre in Paris which he said would spread Japan's spirit throughout Europe.

"This great vessel of glass, metal and light...must be a lively space for encounters and exchanges, a window open onto Japanese society, genius and future," Chirac, a Japanese art lover, said as he opened the centre together with Princess Sayako.
Quoting writer Andre Malraux, the late culture minister of General Charles de Gaulle, he said France wanted to be "the messenger of Japanese genius to the whole western world".
The elegant building, financed by Japanese public and private funds, was built on the banks of the Seine river near the Eiffel Tower on land loaned for 60 years by the French state.
